title: Transparent request fingerprinting + lease-based coalescing to eliminate retry-driven duplicate charges
creator: Marcus Li
description:
Problem: Customers are still seeing sporadic duplicate charges when client SDKs retry requests due to transient network timeouts or perceived server errors. Current approaches (opaque replay tokens, single-ack windows, optimistic reservations) reduce but do not eliminate edge-level inflight duplication, particularly for short-running requests that race across retries and behind global load balancers.

Proposal: Implement a transparent request fingerprinting and short-lease coalescing mechanism at the edge/ingest proxy. The system will: 1) derive a deterministic request fingerprint from client-supplied idempotency hints (when available) plus normalized request attributes; 2) attempt to acquire a short-lived lease in a fast in-memory lease store (Redis cluster with cross-AZ replication); 3) if the lease is held by another in-flight request, coalesce the retry onto the existing execution and return the original response (or a streaming relay) instead of charging again; 4) create a provisional billing reservation tied to the lease that only converts to a final charge once the canonical execution completes and is acknowledged by the accounting pipeline.

Why different from existing patterns: This design combines lightweight deterministic fingerprinting with an explicit short lease window and active coalescing — not merely dedupe at ingestion or post-hoc reconciliation. It is optimized for low-latency, high-throughput edge behavior and reduces the need for complex reconciliation sweeps for common retry scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Edge: fingerprint generation must add <3ms p50 latency to ingest path for typical text-gen requests
Accounting: duplicate charges caused by two-concurrent-retries for same logical request reduced to <0.1% in synthetic retry tests
Coalescing: when a retry arrives within lease window it attaches to the leader execution and does not create a second consumption event
Resilience: lease expiry and leader failure paths are documented and covered by integration tests
Feature flag: rollout controllable per-customer and per-region; defaults off
Metrics: dashboards for lease-acquire success, coalesce-rate, provisional-reservations, conversion-latency, and reconciliation errors
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Fingerprint entropy: prefer deterministic canonicalization of request payloads + client id hint over trusting client-provided idempotency keys alone; avoids client bugs but may under-dedupe when payload differs slightly
Lease duration: short (100ms-2s) window to balance coalescing effectiveness vs blocking unrelated retries; tunable per-workload
In-memory leases vs durable ledger: use fast in-memory for low latency coalescing; persistent ledger used for final accounting to ensure durability
Provisional billing reservations: create a reversible reservation at lease acquire to prevent immediate double-charge yet allow quick rollback if leader fails
Coalescing semantics: return canonical leader response to attached retries; for streaming endpoints we will relay the same stream to all attached clients where feasible
Backpressure: coalescing must not amplify head-of-line blocking; if leader execution is slow, later retries may opt out of coalescing after a configurable timeout
implementation_outline: Edge/ingest proxy: add fingerprinting layer and lease client; try-acquire lease on request ingress
Lease store: Redis cluster with local read-replicas for latency; lease entries store fingerprint, leader instance id, provisional reservation id, and lease expiry timestamp
Coalescer: lightweight in-proxy coalescer to attach duplicate inflight requests to leader's response stream or completion future
Accounting path: provisional reservation emitted to billing queue; final conversion emitted after canonical execution completes and confirmation from core accounting service
Failure handling: if leader dies before completion, lease invalidated and attached clients receive retry instructions; provisional reservations are released and do not convert to charges
Observability: expose lease metrics, coalesce rates, reservation lifecycle traces, and sample request traces for postmortem analysis
Feature gating: rollout via feature flag service with per-customer overrides; telemetry to detect any regressions early
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable for 5 internal customers in us-east-1; monitor coalesce-rate and errors for 48 hours
Stage 2 (scaled canary): enable for top 50 customers with high retry rates and non-critical SLAs; run 1-week soak
Stage 3 (gradual): 10% increments by customer cohort over two weeks, then global opt-in
Fallback: feature flag off triggers immediate removal of lease checks; system falls back to existing provisional-reservation + reconciliation behavior
testing_plan: Unit: fingerprint canonicalization tests, lease acquisition/release edge cases
Integration: simulate concurrent duplicate retries under load; verify only one compute invocation and one final charge
Chaos: leader process kill while coalesced requests are attached; verify recovery and no ghost charges
Load: perf test for ingress latency impact at 10k rps with varying request sizes
E2E: billing pipeline tests where provisional reservation converted or released depending on outcome
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: lease_acquire_latency, lease_acquire_failure_rate, coalesce_rate, provisional_reservation_count, reservation_conversion_latency
Alerts: >0.5% increase in duplicate-charge incidents vs baseline; lease-store error rate >0.1%
SLO: coalescing should not increase 99th percentile ingest latency by more than 10ms when enabled
migration_notes: Backward compatibility: clients without idempotency hints still get fingerprinted from normalized payloads; fallback may have lower dedupe yield
Data retention: lease entries expire automatically; billing reservations follow existing retention rules
Reconciliation: keep existing post-hoc reconciliation sweep as a safety net for rare failure modes
Operational runbook: step-by-step for lease-store failover, how to safely flip feature flag off, and how to investigate suspected duplicate-charge incidents
security_considerations: Fingerprinting must avoid including sensitive PII/raw prompt content in telemetry; only store hashed canonicalized signatures
Lease store access restricted to edge proxies and accounting services via mTLS and IAM
Provisional reservation tokens are short-lived and encrypted at rest
Design reviewed by security team and KMS/PKI owners before canary
Audit logs: every lease acquire/release/coalesce event recorded for later forensic analysis
